 Judgment

1. This is an appeal preferred by the appellant Prem Singh Tomar assailing the impugned order dated 08.04.2021, whereby he has been convicted for selling food article (Khoya) meant for human consumption in terms of Section 26(1) and 26(2)(ii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the FSS Act, 2006") read with Section 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006.
2. At the outset, it may be pointed out no one has appeared for the appellant to press the present appeal or to address arguments.
Having heard the Ld. Chief PP for the respondent and on perusal of the record, I proceed to decide the present appeal.

sentences.text:
Briefly stated, the appellant stated that on 05.03.2020 at about 09:00 AM, Smt. Shalley Chauhan,
the then Food Safety Officer (in short "the FSO") along with Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant, as per office order/directions and under supervision of Sh. Hukam Singh, Designated Officer (DO) of District Central visited the premises of M/s Prem Mawa Bhandar, Gate No. 2, Mawa Society, Mori Gate (Khoya Auction Site), Delhi110006 and the appellant was found conducting the business at the aforesaid premises and storing and selling food article "Khoya" meant for human consumption.

entities.text: Mawa Society, Mori Gate (Khoya Auction Site)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the course of such inspection, the samples were collected and divided equally into four counterparts by putting them into four clean and dry glass bottles with twenty drops of formalin in each counterpart of the sample; and one of the counterpart of the sample was sent to the Food Analyst, Govt. of NCT of Delhi on 06.03.2020.

The Food Analyst vide Report No. FSS/451/2018 dated 19.03.2020 submitted the report, which is as under:
"The sample is substandard because milk fat of dried matter and ReichertMeissl value are less than the prescribed minimum limits of 30.0% and 28.0 respectively and ButyroRefractometer reading at 40 Deg C exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 43.0."
4.

In a nutshell, the complaint was filed by the FSO as per Rule 3.1.1(3) of the FSS Rules, 2011 and notice was issued to the appellant and on his appearance on 15.02.2021, he was supplied with the copy of the complaint and other annexures.
On 11.03.2021, the appellant submitted his written submissions in which inter alia he pleaded guilty for his act and undertook that he would not repeat the wrongful act in future.

5. Suffice to state that as the appellant pleaded guilty and conceded that he was on the wrong side of the law, vide the impugned order dated 08.04.2021, the appellant was convicted u/s 26(1) and 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006 for being in violation of Regulation No.
2.4.6 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations,
2011 making it punishable u/s 51 of the FSS Act, 2006.
6.

sentences.text:
After hearing the appellant, the Ld. AO/ADM was pleased to impose penalty of Rs.1,50,000/,
which is assailed in the present appeal.

7. The main grievance of the appellant is that he is an illiterate person and could not understand the meaning of pleading guilty and merely accepted that he was guilty on the suggestion given by the Court staff of the concerned designated authority.
8. I am afraid that the present appeal is devoid of any merit.
At the cost of repetition, the appellant submitted a written reply in his handwriting and duly signed by him whereby he pleaded guilty.

The appellant had been supplied with all the relevant documents concerning the complaint on 15.02.2021 and at the cost of repetition, when he appeared on 11.03.2021, he submitted a written reply inter alia pleading guilty and apologizing besides undertaking not to repeat the wrongful act in future.
In such eventuality, the appellant has a limited right so as to challenge the quantum of the sentence in terms of Section 375 of the CrPC.

It is pertinent to mention here that the maximum penalty by way of fine is Rs.5.00 Lakh and, therefore, it prima facie appears that the Ld. AO/ADM Sh. Prem Singh Tomar vs Food Safety Officer on 1 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642152/
2 has imposed a reasonable and fair monetary penalty upon the appellant, considering that he was the first defaulter in respect of the relevant Regulation.

10. Record of the AO/ADM along with copy of the judgment be sent back with the direction to realize the fine from the appellant.
11. Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
